grade.rationale: The command is generally clear and handles expected operational failures consistently, but its mode validation has a concrete gap and its hard-coded collaborators make orchestration behavior unnecessarily difficult to test in isolation.

summary: The implementation is readable and mostly robust. The main correctness issue is that an explicitly supplied `--last 1` is accepted alongside `--base`, despite those options representing mutually exclusive modes. Testability is also reduced by constructing every reviewer, provider, and service directly inside `RunAsync`. No coverage conclusions were drawn because coverage data is unavailable.

grade.rationale: Core control flow and exit-code behavior are coherent, but explicit use of `--last 1` bypasses the intended provider-mode exclusivity check.
Names and flow are understandable, though argument parsing relies on default values to represent both absence and explicit input, and orchestration is tightly coupled to concrete implementations.
Usage text, validation messages, and result formatting are generally clear; the accepted behavior for `--base` combined with `--last 1` contradicts the documented command modes.
Expected invocation, Git/review, filesystem, and authorization failures are converted into a consistent diagnostic and error exit code, while cancellation remains able to propagate.
Parsing can be exercised indirectly, but successful orchestration paths require real concrete service, provider, and reviewer implementations because there are no injection seams.

findings.title: Explicit `--last 1` bypasses mutually exclusive mode validation
findings.description: The parser stores only the numeric value of `--last`, whose default is also `1`. Consequently, `--base <commit> --last 1` passes this condition even though the error message and usage syntax establish `--base` and `--last` as different provider modes. This makes validation depend on the supplied value rather than whether the option was present.
findings.recommendation: Track whether `--last` was explicitly supplied, such as with a `lastSet` boolean, and reject any explicit `--last` whenever `--base` is present regardless of its value.

findings.title: Command orchestration is coupled to concrete dependencies
findings.description: `RunAsync` directly constructs the agent adapter, review service, and Git provider. Unit tests therefore cannot substitute deterministic fakes to cover success, regression, empty-result, JSON, and collaborator-failure paths without invoking repository-facing implementations.
findings.recommendation: Move the orchestration into an internal overload or instance command that accepts the change-set provider, review service, and reviewer factory as dependencies, while retaining the current public method as the production composition root.
